newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks set for sharp rally after Wall St rise.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks set for sharp rally after Wall St rise.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks look set for a sharp rally on Wednesday following a surge in U.S. share prices overnight, brokers said.
The Dow industrials posted their second biggest point gain in history in Tuesday, rising 173.38 points to 6,833.59.
"Generally today I think we will see the market up quite sharply," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.
"We still need to break through that 12,850 level before we can confirm a technical breakout. That is really the main feature of the day, whether we can break through 12,850 or not."
The Hang Seng Index fell 45.19 points to 12,580.85 on Tuesday.
Later, the Hang Seng London Reference Index of Hong Kong stocks traded in London rose 17.47 points to 12,598.32.
Dharmala Securities director of research Ben Kwong said the rally on Wall Street could propel the index to 12,700 on Wednesday.

"The Hong Kong stock market has already consolidated for a while at low levels so the better performance of Wall Street provides an excuse for local investors to push the index up to higher levels," he said. "The long bond yield is also softening and that will help interest rate sensitive stocks."
He said the index could test 12,800 points in coming days.
